description: The provider reuses the processed state of an exact prompt prefix seen recently, billing cached input tokens at a discount and lowering time to first token.
The part of a prompt identical across requests (tools, system prompt, static examples). Put it first and varying content last.
The share of input tokens served from the cache, read from usage data. The only proof caching works.
Asynchronous processing of many requests within a window (commonly 24 hours) at a large discount, with separate throughput limits.
Returning a stored answer when a new question is similar enough to a past one, skipping the model. Risks: false hits, staleness, cross-user leaks.
Caching the response of a deterministic call keyed by the exact prompt version and inputs. No similarity threshold to tune.
